title: What you must be able to whiteboard in an AI architect interview
oneliner: Be ready to whiteboard three things: the agent orchestration flow, state/memory/tool selection, and the security and governance design.
says: AI architect interviews may ask you to whiteboard. The key areas: agent orchestration flow - how multiple agents communicate and how you achieve the use case with a multi-agent workflow; state management, memory, and tool selection - how agents maintain state and choose tools for a task; and the security and governance design of the AI agent system.
explained: Whiteboarding tests whether your knowledge is structural or recited. Anyone can list agent frameworks; drawing the orchestration flow forces you to show who calls whom, what state travels, and where failures surface. That is why interviewers use it - the diagram cannot be memorized.

His three areas are well chosen because they are the three places agent systems actually fail. Orchestration failures: agents looping or deadlocking. State and tool failures: agents forgetting context or picking the wrong tool. Governance failures: agents taking actions nobody authorized. Prepare one real architecture you have built or studied, and practice drawing all three views of it until each takes two minutes.
takeaway: Interview prep = three drawings from memory: orchestration flow, state/memory/tool choices, and the governance boundary around it all.
